tools.name: intake_gadget
tools.description: Return four hardware-planning intake questions covering placement, interaction, room sensing and budget, with answer options and their planning meanings. No input.

tools.name: plan_gadget
tools.description: Deterministically plan a physical body for an AI agent using Meta Muse boards. Partial intake answers produce remaining questions and an intake completion status. Inputs: `idea` 3-2000 chars (optional when `answers` or `needs` are given); `answers` {size, interaction, sensing, budget} using the intake option values; `platform` one of muse-esp32, muse-linux, any (default any); `budget_usd` number greater than 0, up to 100000; `owned_device_ids` up to 50 catalog ids; `needs` values: voice, screen, images, touch, camera, air-sensors, e-ink, battery, round, home-tunnel, big-screen, compute, linux; `size` one of pocket, desk, wall, hidden, any (default any); `limit` 1-5 (default 3). Boards that meet the hard needs and the budget rank first, cheapest first. Returns fit, notes, warnings, intake status, questions, picks with difficulty, terms and next steps.

idea.description: Gadget idea or use case, 3-2000 characters. Optional when `answers` or `needs` are given.

size.description: Where should this body live? pocket = Pocket; desk = Desk; wall = Wall or fridge; hidden = Hidden, no screen.

interaction.description: How should you interact with it? voice = Talk to it; touch = Touch screen; light-button = Light and button.

sensing.description: Should it sense the room? camera = Camera; air-quality = Air quality; none = None.

budget.description: What budget should I plan around? under-25 = Under $25; under-50 = Under $50; under-100 = Under $100; no-limit = No limit.

answers.description: The human's intake answers, by question id, using the option values from intake_gadget.

platform.description: Platform filter: muse-esp32, muse-linux, or any. Default any.

budget_usd.description: Optional hardware budget in USD. Must be greater than 0, max 100000.

owned_device_ids.description: Catalog device ids the user already owns. Max 50.

needs.description: Optional explicit needs. Allowed: voice, screen, images, touch, camera, air-sensors, e-ink, battery, round, home-tunnel, big-screen, compute, linux.

size.description: Preferred size or placement: pocket, desk, wall, hidden, any. Default any.

limit.description: Number of picks to return: 1-5, default 3.

tools.name: get_build_plan
tools.description: Return the complete deterministic build plan for a catalog device id: difficulty, board-specific flash warnings, parts, shopping list with buy_options, prices checked date and purchase policy, steps, machine-readable assembly with verify checks, commands, links, caveats and an agent-ready brief. Input: `device_id` 1-200 chars.

tools.name: assess_hackability
tools.description: Look up a device by id, exact name or substring and return hackability, brick risk, firmware links, curated firmware playbooks, community size, build page and agent platform support. Input: `device_name` 1-200 chars.

tools.name: find_reverse_engineering_examples
tools.description: Search Hackshop's curated hardware reverse-engineering examples and research methods. With no query, returns the newest dated examples first. Evidence labels distinguish reproduced work, documented implementations, author demos and analysis methods; they do not imply compatibility with similar-looking hardware.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive search across title, device, exact models, summary, outcome and tags. Empty returns the latest examples.

use_case.description: Filter source-backed design starters by intended use.

max_device_price_usd.description: Maximum lowest-listed device price in USD; unknown prices excluded. Accessories, host, shipping and tax are extra; availability is returned separately.

tools.name: find_firmware_playbooks
tools.description: Find curated owner-authorized firmware, local-protocol and cloud-replacement playbooks. Results rank less-invasive paths first and contain research guidance rather than device compatibility approval.

tools.name: check_firmware_compatibility
tools.description: Fail-closed compatibility check for one firmware playbook. Required model, codename, revision, SoC or firmware identifiers must exactly match a curated target; missing facts return unknown and mismatches return unsupported.

model_number.description: Model number from the physical label, not the retail family name.

sensor.description: Confirmed image sensor or other sensor identifier.

wifi_module.description: Confirmed Wi-Fi or radio module identifier.

tools.name: get_firmware_playbook
tools.description: Return a curated firmware playbook with exact targets, prerequisites, backups, recovery, independent risk axes, sources, validation checks and the human-only destructive-action boundary.

tools.name: verify_firmware_artifact
tools.description: Compare a caller-supplied filename, source URL and SHA-256 with Hackshop's curated metadata. Hackshop does not fetch, upload or redistribute the artifact; absent hashes return unknown.

tools.name: prepare_firmware_job
tools.description: Prepare a non-executing firmware manifest after owner authorization and an exact compatibility match. Returns backup, recovery, sources, validation and stop points; never returns a flash command.

model_number.description: Model number from the physical label, not the retail family name.

sensor.description: Confirmed image sensor or other sensor identifier.

wifi_module.description: Confirmed Wi-Fi or radio module identifier.
